dedupe_keys.name: national travel survey england department for transport

description: The National Travel Survey (NTS) is the Department for Transport's household survey of personal travel, the primary source on travel patterns of residents of England. It records where people travel from and to, distance, purpose, mode and time, together with personal and socio-economic details, car availability and licence holding. Surveys ran periodically from 1965 and continuously since July 1988; from 2002 the sample rose to about 15,000 addresses a year, and it was enlarged again in 2023. DfT uses it as core base data for its transport models and scheme appraisal, and publishes annual statistics on GOV.UK, most recently the 2025 edition on 10 September 2026. Microdata for 2002 to 2024 are held by the UK Data Service in three versions: End User Licence files at regional level (SNs 5340 and 6108) for registered users, Special Licence files at local authority level (SNs 7553 and 7804), and a Secure Access version with postcode sectors (SN 7559) that requires training. Formats include SPSS, Stata and tab-delimited files; the data are Crown copyright and free for registered users. Caveats: short walks were under-recorded in 2002 and 2003, the 2020 and 2021 samples were small and methods changed during the pandemic, and 2024 SPSS and Stata files lack labels. The survey supports demand modelling, capacity planning and agent-based travel simulation; related records are MATSim and the Glasgow Huq origin-destination matrices.
